findings.title: Rejected devices are cached in localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)`. When the device limit has been reached, the first request from a new device fails with `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but its device key is still stored in `localCache` for 29 minutes. On the very next HTTP request from that same device, `a.localCache.Get(key)` returns a cache hit and `tagDeviceUI` returns `nil` without querying the store, allowing `Anonymous.Authenticate` to succeed and bypassing `AnonymousDeviceLimit`. `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` should only be called after `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` succeeds (and `untagDevice` should also evict the key from `localCache` when a device is deleted on login).

findings.title: Missing test coverage for updating an existing device when at the device limit
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` verifies that a second distinct device is rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `deviceLimit` is 1, but does not verify that calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` again for the already-registered device (`"32mdo31deeqwes"`) succeeds via `updateDevice` once the limit has been reached.
